points.description: Explains the effect on Paul: learning Mr. Leonard's background (he was a champion hurdler who struggled with reading/schoolwork and lost his scholarship) makes Paul relate to/empathize with him, or see him as someone like himself, or motivates Paul to want to help him.

Supports with a relevant detail from the story, e.g. Paul recognizes the feelings as familiar (embarrassment when reading aloud), or Paul says 'It's time to start your training' to help Mr. Leonard in return, or Mr. Leonard's struggle with reading/failing college.

rubric.notes: Full marks: a clear effect on Paul (empathy/connection and wanting to help Mr. Leonard in return) plus a supporting story detail. One mark if the effect is stated without any detail, or a detail is given without explaining the effect. Equivalent wording is accepted.
